description: Orchestrator event-loop internal parameters (Python OrchestratorConfig knobs not part of the user-facing orchestrator section). Loaded from orchestrator.json if not inlined.

ep_gpu_indices.description: LEGACY-LOOP ONLY (TD-ORCH-EP-GPU-INDICES-DEAD): EP owner set for the FETCH_AND_RUN_MOE round-robin — GPU positions (index into hardware.gpus[], INV-4.18) allowed to OWN routed experts — honored ONLY by drivers that build the legacy OrchestratorLoop from this config (engine_glue.ep_gpu_indices_from_config; e.g. tools/elb_train). The PRODUCTION orchestrator (Orchestrator.boot) does NOT honor it — it derives expert hosts from hardware.gpus roles and the daemon's REEF placement picks per-expert owners — and REFUSES to boot a config that sets it non-empty (a silently-discarded owner set masqueraded as a live bisect lever in the EP4 investigation). Empty (DEFAULT) = derive from topology. HAZARD (INV-FAR deadline-burn): MUST exclude GPUs that host no expert cache — e.g. a dspark draft GPU — an expert round-robined onto such a GPU can never become ready, and every MoE layer then burns the full FETCH_AND_RUN fetch deadline.

prefill_sc_min_tokens.description: SC small-prefill downgrade threshold: a superchunk-path prefill whose DELTA (tokens actually prefilled after any prefix-cache hit) is STRICTLY BELOW this runs the ordinary chunked path at prefill_sc_small_chunk_tokens rows instead — a whole-delta MOE_BIG union sweep on a small delta (a short follow-up turn on a cached prefix) evicts the decode-warmed expert cache for no amortization win. 0 = off (everything superchunk, pre-2026-08-26 behavior). Default 256: below one superchunk stride, and small enough that the champion long-prompt prefill numbers (glm_prefill.md 44.6/43.6/42.4 tok/s @ 8k/20k/25k, cold cache => delta >= 256) route identically. A downgraded delta's chunk shapes differ from an uncached superchunk run's — the accepted bf16 batch-width shape class of TD-SERVE-SC-TRAJECTORY. Adaptive successor: TD-SC-SMALL-PREFILL-ADAPTIVE.

prefill_sc_small_chunk_tokens.description: Chunk rows a below-threshold (prefill_sc_min_tokens) delta is prefilled at — deliberately SMALL so experts are touched in per-chunk unions the resident expert cache can absorb, independent of orchestrator.prefill_chunk_tokens (which union-saturating recipes carry at 512). Clamped to min(512, EngineInfo.moe_batch_capacity) at boot. Default 64 = the GLM test-proven stride.

degraded_retry_enabled.description: Serving-level retry of a DEGRADED request (TD-V4-FIRSTREQ-COLD-SHARE-OVER-CAPACITY option (d)): when a request completes with RequestStats.moe_degraded_layers > 0 (some MoE layer finalized with an INCOMPLETE expert set -- the measured V4 tp2/ep4 first-request-after-boot shape), the orchestrator re-runs it instead of returning a known-wrong answer -- provided NOTHING was streamed to the client: a prefill-degraded attempt is abandoned BEFORE its first token (so streaming requests are covered by the retry), while a request that degraded only during decode with tokens already streamed is delivered flagged and counted (degraded_unretryable), never silently re-run. false = deliver degraded results immediately (they still carry the WARNING, the per-request moe_degraded_layers stat, and never register prefix holders). Every retry is logged with boot totals so a box that degrades CONSTANTLY is visible instead of silently doubling its latency -- watch degraded_retries on [orch-stats] and the delivered-degraded total in the WARNING line.

degraded_retry_max.description: Maximum serving-level re-runs of ONE degraded request (bounds the added latency to (1+max) prefills worst-case). Default 1: the V4 first-request degrade is SELF-CORRECTING -- once anything is resident, residency-aware routing stops over-assigning the draft GPU -- so a single retry lands on warm residency (measured clean on the 2026-08-27 cold-boot repro, scratchpad/td_degraded_serve.log). 0 behaves like degraded_retry_enabled=false. A request still degraded after max retries is delivered flagged, with the retry count on its [orch-stats] line.

kvxp_large_prefill_tokens.description: 44z bounded large-prefill wait, threshold half (TD-KVXP-PER-STEP-FLOOR; Python orchestrator, read at Orchestrator boot): a prefill whose prompt length is >= this many tokens may wait -- bounded by kvxp_large_prefill_wait_ms -- for the expert-zone rebalancer's eager background drain after a pool-pressure admission refusal, then re-issue. Short prefills and decode steps NEVER wait. 0 DISABLES the wait. Default 8192, derived: drains are tick-bound 200-600 ms vs measured prefill rates 88.8-140 tok/s, so a >= ~6,600-token prompt keeps one drain under ~1% of TTFT. Only engaged when the rebalancer itself is enabled (_internal-kv_expert_rebalance.enabled / LS_KV_EXPERT_REBALANCE) -- without it no drain is coming and waiting would only delay the 500. Env override: LS_KVXP_LARGE_PREFILL_TOKENS (either way).

kvxp_large_prefill_wait_ms.description: 44z bounded large-prefill wait, per-request wall budget in ms (see kvxp_large_prefill_tokens). A cap on FUTILE waiting, not the typical cost: the measured miss was ~200 ms and the default 2000 ms covers >= 3 drain periods; each engine-side claim stays all-or-nothing with full rollback (the wait sits ABOVE the admission protocol -- INV-KDA-STATE (a) untouched). 0 disables the wait. Env override: LS_KVXP_LARGE_PREFILL_WAIT_MS (either way).
